responses.sq_001: In May 2026 I co-produced a student society TikTok from a written event brief. I wrote the 18-second script, planned the shot list, filmed with two teammates, and revised the opening after a rehearsal. The post reached 22,400 views and a 12.1% engagement rate; the dated brief and analytics are available.
responses.sq_002: On that project I turned the brief into three hooks, reviewed them with the event lead, selected one, drafted a storyboard, assigned filming roles, rehearsed, filmed, and logged the approved takes for the editor.
responses.sq_003: I shared the storyboard two days early. The event lead said the first scene did not name the audience problem, so I rewrote that scene, showed the revised version, and received approval before filming.
responses.sq_004: When our microphone failed on shoot day, I cut the script from four scenes to two, moved indoors, used a borrowed phone microphone, and still delivered the approved footage before the 4 pm deadline.
responses.sq_005: For three posts in one week, I previously maintained a shared board with one row per script, named an owner and approval deadline, batched filming into one session, and sent each draft to the lead before scheduling.

responses.sq_003: I shared the first script in our group chat. A teammate asked for a clearer call to action, so I changed the final line and checked the revision with the group before filming.
responses.sq_004: We had one afternoon and one phone. I reduced the location changes, prepared props before the team arrived, and completed the planned shots in two hours.
responses.sq_005: I would keep three scripts in a shared checklist, agree approval times with the lead, and batch similar shots. I have not yet delivered three professional posts in one week.
